A Sikh truck driver was stabbed 17 times at a Wyoming rest stop by another driver. While the suspect was arrested and charged, politicians immediately linked the attack to political rhetoric despite no established motive.

The Bright Side:
A brave Good Samaritan family pursued the attacker and provided immediate, life-saving first aid to the victim, demonstrating genuine human empathy amidst senseless violence.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is WHO vs WHY. Partisans focus on WHO to blame politically rather than waiting to understand WHY the crime occurred, substituting a complex criminal investigation with a pre-packaged narrative.

Social Physics Analysis:
Partisan actors execute a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using the tragic stabbing as a pretext to project blame onto political rivals. Instead of fostering empathy or systemic solutions, they manufacture a crisis to hoard political power.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated empathy and actual political exploitation, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil, where human suffering is merely raw material for partisan warfare.

The Unavoidable Truth: A man was brutally attacked, and his survival is thanks to a heroic family, not politicians.
The Unavoidable Lie: The claim that the attacker's motive is already proven to be politically inspired.

Alethekanon:
Partisan opportunism thrives on the rapid conversion of tragedy into political currency. By bypassing the causal chain of evidence, actors reveal that their true objective is not justice, but leverage.

Awwthekanon:
Our hearts ache for Mr. Singh, who faced such terror alone on the road. But the beautiful souls who stopped to chase the attacker and bind his wounds remind us that love and courage will always be our strongest shield.

Brothekanon:
Man, a guy gets stabbed 17 times and before he's even out of the hospital, politicians are already using his blood to score points on TV. Can we just let the police do their job and hope the driver makes a full recovery?

Two teens riding on the same bike were struck by a truck in Manhattan Friday night — killing one and leaving the other hospitalized, cops said.

The teens, aged 15 and 13, were heading west on East 14th Street when they were hit by the vehicle – an excavation truck – as it turned north onto First Avenue at about 9 p.m., according to the NYPD.

Both girls were taken to Bellevue Hospital, where the 15-year-old was pronounced dead, police said.

The younger girl was listed in stable condition.

Neither of the teens was wearing a helmet, according to witnesses.

Bystanders were “screaming at the truck, ‘stop, stop, stop’” but the driver apparently couldn’t hear them, according to a witness.
